summary: ```# Marvelous Designer Official - Ten-Minute Beginner's Tutorial: Drop Shoulder Hoodie ## Introduction In this tutorial, we will learn how to create a drop shoulder hoodie using Marvelous Designer. The following steps outline the processes involved, from importing models to adjusting patterns and sewing techniques. ## Importing Models To make Lianmaoshan more convenient, please first import the basic T-shape file and the female downward line VR virtual model with the hole window. ## Activating Simulation Then press the Control key to activate the simulation and place the T-shirt on the virtual model. ## Checking Costume Fit Select the transparent image to check if the costume fits. Comparing to the virtual model, the shoulder line of the costume is too short for the loose style of the costume. ## Adjusting the Shoulder Line 1. Press the Control key and point the shoulder line of the front and back slices out along the slope, then press the right key. 2. Enter 60 mm in the moving distance spring. 3. Since the shoulder length has been increased, the highest point of the sleeve should be lowered by 30 mm to match the modification. ## Editing the Sleeve Curve 1. Select the editor curve point tool and delete the point higher than the curve of the sleeve. 2. Add two straight lines to draw a short straight line. 3. As the curve of the sleeve is very smooth, please adjust the hemline of the body plate as well. Keep the corner of the corner as straight as possible to avoid sharp corners after cutting. ## Merging Front and Back Slices 1. Select the front and middle lines. 2. In the menu on the right, select "Merge" to merge the two front slices as a whole. 3. Use the same operation for the back slices. ## Adjusting Length and Width 1. Increase the bottom line to shorten the length of the costume. 2. Select the bottom line and select the inner line of the shoulder line in the menu on the right. 3. Enter 45 mm in the shoulder line and click OK. 4. Press the right key on the inner line and select the cut seam in the menu to remove the body plate slices from the bottom. ## Modifying Waist and Body Plate 1. Select the side bottom point and move it out 30 mm to widen the waist. 2. Move the middle line of the body plate down 30 mm. 3. Then select the editor curve point tool to change the straight line to a curve line. 4. Click on the line section and drag the curve point to adjust. ## Final Adjustments 1. Move the bottom point of the sleeve to the outside 15 mm to increase the chest of the front and back slices. 2. Remove unnecessary points for the seam and move the seam line to increase the length of the sleeve. 3. Due to the 3D grid, it may break when extending, please rearrange the plate and simulate. ## Setting Length for the Sleeve Plate 1. The seam is too wide; use the length tool to change it. 2. Set the length to 280 mm, choose BOSE in the direction, and start from the middle to calculate the length to the two ends. 3. Since we will cut a sleeve plate from the sleeve plate, we can make it longer using the inner thread to create the cut line of the sleeve plate. ## Creating the Sleeve Seam Line 1. Then select the cut seam in the window to automatically create the seam line. 2. Click the point with the longer thread, then select the point with the shorter thread, and click it with the right button. 3. Select the right one in the menu, and then select the left or right one according to the need to ensure that the upper and lower threads have the same length. ## Narrowing the Plate 1. Drag the selection box to narrow the plate. 2. Activate the simulation; the sleeve plate will become wider. 3. Freeze the sleeve plate to maintain the shape and adjust the sleeve to be longer. ## Creating a Hat Plate 1. Create a 500 mm wide, 500 mm high rectangular plate and arrange it on the side of the model's head. 2. Change the shape type to flat, which will help us create a simpler hat plate. 3. Use the 3D plate tool to open the transparency preview. Click the plate to draw the line according to the model's head curve. ## Finalizing the Hat Shape 1. Press the Control key to create the curve, then click the starting point to complete the closed shape. 2. Select the 3D tool to edit the line and choose cut in the menu. 3. Remove unnecessary curve points and change some straight lines to curve points to make the curve smoother. ## Adjusting the Hat 1. Choose a clear line on one side of the model and check the length using the property editor. 2. Drag the line in the back of the hat to match the bottom line and the size of the previous measurement. 3. Adjust the curve in the back according to the video. ## Creating a Symmetrical Plate 1. Create a symmetrical plate using the positioning ball tool to move it to the other side of the head. 2. Select the line sewing tool to create a sewing line. 3. Use the free sewing tool to click the starting point along the moving mouse of the sewing line, then click on the end position. ## Adjusting the Hat Fit 1. If the hat looks too tight, you can move the points on the plate or adjust the line to increase the plate. 2. Adjust the angle to a right angle to ensure that the sewing line is smooth after sewing. 3. Press the Control key to drag the top point of the hat along the line to change the length. ## Conclusion We suggest choosing the way of adjusting the point, not the whole line, to maintain the original curve effect. Finally, drag the hat to the back of the virtual model and adjust the shape to achieve the appropriate effect. To remove the hat, press the Control key on the top of the virtual model and adjust the draw accordingly. ## Adding Pockets 1. Select the front piece; in the menu on the right-hand side, select the pocket from the outside. 2. Cut the pocket from the pocket on the plate of the pocket. 3. Now we have a pocket plate that is automatically arranged on the outside of the original plate. ## Sewing the Pocket You can use a free sewing tool or a line sewing tool to sew the pocket plate to the inner line. In the drawing window, find the Materials file, then drag the knit cord, cotton cord, and jersey fabric to the current fabric maker to use it. Thank you for following along! ```
